title: Read an annotation type's retention

blocks.text: An annotation type's retention is itself an annotation, `@Retention`, and it is RUNTIME-retained, so reflection can read it from the annotation's class object. The page's key points: **with no `@Retention` the policy is CLASS**, not RUNTIME, and the stages nest as `SOURCE < CLASS < RUNTIME`, so **a longer retention includes the shorter stages**.

items: `policyOf(Class<? extends Annotation> type)`: the retention policy of `type`.

`availableIn(Class<? extends Annotation> type, RetentionPolicy stage)`: whether an annotation of `type` still exists at `stage` (`SOURCE` = in the source, `CLASS` = in the `.class` file, `RUNTIME` = to reflection).

cases.says: @Deprecated is RUNTIME, @Override is SOURCE, and an annotation declared with @Retention(CLASS) is CLASS.
An annotation type with no @Retention has the default policy CLASS.
A RUNTIME annotation is also available in the source and the class file, and a CLASS one in the source, but a CLASS one is not available at run time.

concepts: An annotation type without @Retention has the default policy CLASS, so reflection cannot see it.
Retention stages nest as SOURCE < CLASS < RUNTIME, and an annotation type's own @Retention can be read from its class object.
